identity.title: The JCMT Transient Survey: An Extraordinary Submillimeter Flare in the T Tauri Binary System JW 566

paper_type_evidence.quote: The binary T Tauri system JW 566 in the Orion Molecular Cloud underwent an energetic, short-lived flare observed at submillimetre wavelengths by the SCUBA-2 instrument on 26 November 2016 (UT).
The source is detected in a 3 $\mathrm{\:mm}$ continuum image obtained by ALMA on 2015-12-26 ((cite: hacar2018); see Figure [6](#fig:ALMA)).

findings_qualitative.value: Possibly the most luminous known YSO flare and the first coronal flare discovered at sub-mm wavelengths

evidence.quote: The event may be the most luminous known flare associated with a young stellar object and is also the first coronal flare discovered at sub-mm wavelengths.

claims.hypothesis: The JW 566 sub-mm brightening is a short-lived, non-thermal flare
claims.experiment: Light curve in nine sub-intervals, 2-band spectral index, brightness temperature
claims.result: Flux fell from 773 to 400 mJy/beam in 31 min; alpha = 0.11; Tb > 6e4 K

evidence.quote: The flat spectral index, the short variability timescale, and a large $T_{b}$ strongly indicate the flare is a result of gyrosynchrotron/synchrotron emission

claims.hypothesis: The flare is exceptionally luminous compared with other YSO flares
claims.experiment: Compared Lnu at 850 um with GMR-A at 86 GHz
claims.result: 8e19 vs 3e19 erg/s/Hz, about an order of magnitude greater in nuLnu
claims.finding: Possibly the most luminous YSO flare known

evidence.quote: which makes the JW 566 flare an order of magnitude brighter in terms of $\nu L_{\nu}$

claims.hypothesis: The quiescent emission of JW 566 is faint
claims.experiment: Used ALMA 3 mm flux and extrapolated to 850 um
claims.result: 3 mm flux of 0.6 mJy implies a disk 850 um flux of ~10 mJy
claims.finding: The flare is hundreds of times brighter than quiescent emission

evidence.quote: This presumably-quiescent flux is a factor of $8\times10^{2}$ fainter than the 850 $\mu$m$\,$ continuum measurement of the flare

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Reprocessed accretion luminosity through thermal dust emission ruled out by short decay timescale

evidence.quote: The short timescale for the decay of the flare rules out reprocessed accretion luminosity through thermal dust emission in the envelope

limitations_admitted.value: True flare timescale unknown; no simultaneous data at other wavelengths; no polarimetry

evidence.quote: The true timescale of the flare remains unknown, as there are no data available at other wavelengths during the time of our observation.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single event; the 450 um detection is only SNR 6
Brightness temperature range spans five orders of magnitude
ALMA data play only a minor, quiescent-flux role
Possible CO(3-2) contamination of the 850 um band argued negligible using a coarse map
